Naegele rule and pregnancy dating: 4

A patient has long irregular cycles and asks for an exact delivery date from an unadjusted Naegele calculation. Which limitation must be considered because the conventional formula assumes a different cycle pattern?

  1. 280 days from the first day of the LMP
  2. 17 October 2026
  3. Use the best obstetric estimate, including early ultrasound
  4. Account for cycle length and reliability of menstrual dating
  5. First day of the last menstrual period
Answer and explanation

Account for cycle length and reliability of menstrual dating

A non-28-day or irregular cycle limits an unadjusted LMP estimate.

Option explanations

Account for cycle length and reliability of menstrual dating: A non-28-day or irregular cycle limits an unadjusted LMP estimate.

First day of the last menstrual period: Conventional menstrual dating starts from the first day of the LMP, not the last bleeding day or presumed conception day. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

280 days from the first day of the LMP: The conventional estimate assumes a 28-day cycle and ovulation around day 14. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

17 October 2026: Adding 280 days to 10 January 2026 gives 17 October 2026. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Use the best obstetric estimate, including early ultrasound: First-trimester ultrasound can improve dating when menstrual history is unreliable; formal redating guidance applies. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
